sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises sharply once utilization passes about 72% of the credit limit.
Past delinquencies are the second most important driver, and having at least one delinquency raises the risk of default.
Income is a moderate effect, with higher incomes associated with lower risk of default.
Length of credit history has a weak effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk.
The effect of utilization is roughly the same at every level of income, so the two do not interact in a way the data can detect.

Debt-to-income ratio, applicant age, the two application attributes and recent credit inquiries hardly matter for the predictions, and the data do not settle whether debt-to-income has any effect at all.
The data do not settle whether the effect of past delinquencies grows or shrinks with credit history length.
